newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia to stage Cambodia evacuation -minister.
newsitem.headline: Australia to stage Cambodia evacuation -minister.

text.p: Australia will on Friday evacuate hundreds of Australians, Canadians and New Zealanders from strife-torn Cambodia, Australian Foreign Minister Alexander Downer said on Thursday.

Downer said that while the situation in the Cambodian capital Phnom Penh was calm, the government had decided to offer military evacuation because of growing fears among its nationals in the Southeast Asian state.

Australia has five military C-130 aircraft on standby, two in Malayasia and three in the northern Australian city of Darwin. Downer said the number of aircraft to be sent for the evacuation would depend on demand.
Australian radio reported two planes would be used and Swedish nationals would also be offered evacuation.
"While the situation in the Cambodian capital is now realitvely calm, members of the Australian community are understandably concerned about future uncertainty," Downer said in a statement.

"The government has decided to mount an operation to facilitate the departure of those members of the Australian community and other nationals for whom we are resposible if they wish to leave Phnom Penh," he said.

Downer said Australia recommends that people not involved in essential duties in Cambodia should leave. There are up to 600 Australians in Cambodia, although there was no mention whether Australia was withdrawing diplomatic staff.
Hundreds of Thai and Singaporean nationals have already been evacuated from Cambodia and the United States has said it would be pulling out about 40 diplomats and dependents.
The United States has also urged between 1,000 and 1,300 other Americans in Phnom Penh and elsewhere in Cambodia to leave over the next few days.

Cambodia was thrown into turmoil at the weekend when Second Prime Minister Hun Sen staged a military takeover and grabbed control of the capital in what First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh termed a coup d'etat.
